newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse moves to timid pickup.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse moves to timid pickup.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour trading on Wednesday 0.14 percent higher after some leading stocks resumed activity.
The all-share index closed at 434.57 points from 433.95 points on Tuesday.
"We can say that since Friday the market is picking up gradually. It is a timid but healthy pickup after profit taking dampened activity for three weeks," a broker at Maroc Inter Titres (MIT) said.
SNI,, the country's second largest private conglomerate, fell three dirhams to close at 527 dirhams. The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.5 billion dirhams.
"After having distributed a 10 dirhams dividend on Friday, SNI is still adjusting its value, but I do not think it will keep this trend," he said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private group that holds stakes in more than 100 firms, gained five dirhams at 495 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the largest market capitalisations, was up one dirham to 396 dirhams.
First tranche of privatisation bonds that were issued in January lost five dirhams to close at 1,135 dirhams while second tranche, issued in April, remained unchanged at 1,068 dirhams.
The bonds are negotiable on the bourse or can be swapped for equity in future privatisations.
Traded volume on the bourse was 19 million dirhams.
